newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds pare gains, lack customer interest.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds pare gains, lack customer interest.

text.p: German Bund futures pared gains in late Monday trading but were expected to broadly trade in a range over the next sessions, lacking the momentum to extend gains amassed late last week.
"The long end is firmer, but basically we are not seeing much customer interest in buying. Instead we are rather seeing some sales," said one dealer.
By 1504 GMT the December Bund futures contract had given up all gains, trading down three basis points at the day's low of 97.96 after having touched a session high of 98.19.

Earlier in the session German August wholesale prices, dropping 0.6 percent on the month, together with continued bullish sentiment after Friday's rally, had helped German Bunds move to the session high of 98.19.
But dealers explained that despite earlier forecasts that investors who had missed the rally would be willing to step in at these prices, there was little customer interest.
"We only saw some interest to take some profits," said another Frankfurt dealer.
Although Bunds performed relatively well, the five year Bobl futures contract slipped, dropping eight basis points.

The Bobl contract was trading at 102.86. Dealers explained the softer prices could be a function of the fact that the middle range of the yield curve had performed better over the last week and was overdue for a pull back.
Now dealers expect Bunds will trade in a range, still eyeing the U.S. market for new direction.
